name: Forerunner K2
def: Industrial humanoid listed from about 30,000 dollars, with 52 joints and eleven degree of freedom hands, aimed at factory material handling.
body: Forerunner K2 stands 175 centimetres, weighs 75 kilograms and has 52 degrees of freedom, with each hand offering eleven degrees of freedom, 25 force sensing contact points per finger and a six axis force and torque sensor at the wrist. More than 80 onboard sensors feed compute rated at 100 trillion operations per second, and Kepler quotes millimetre level placement precision. A one hour charge supports up to eight hours of work, helped by joints that draw almost no power when holding a static pose. Kepler demonstrated an eight hour continuous livestreamed work session at the 2025 World Artificial Intelligence Conference and lists the base robot from around 30,000 dollars.
